subject: Edgecase AI — streaming SLOs, traffic profile & cost levers (pilot proposal)
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgecase.ai>, Marta Ruiz <mruiz@edgecase.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edgecase AI — streaming SLOs, traffic profile & cost levers (pilot proposal)

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the Edgecase team. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we have a single action list.

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Latency target: p95 <= 150ms for per-token streaming responses (real-time interactive UI).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 req/s; diurnal peak can hit ~400 req/s for short bursts (10-30m).
- Concurrent user sessions: ~50 concurrent streams during peak.
- Streaming behavior: partial-token streaming with low-latency token emits; server-side KV caching for session context is desirable.

Cost / performance levers we discussed (high level):
1) Continuous batching: aggregate small requests where latency budget allows; dynamic batching windows to reduce per-token GPU cost.
2) KV / prefix caching: cache common session prefixes and reuse KV cache to avoid repeated compute.
3) Quantization profiles: recommend trying int8 quantization for the base model variant; keep a float16 variant for high-quality fallbacks.
4) Model variants & routing: small distilled model for latency-sensitive paths, larger model for quality-sensitive requests; automatic fallback on quality checks.
5) Canary & fallback policies: region-based routing + model fallback when latency SLOs approach breach.

Attachments I dropped into the shared Drive for your review: perf-metrics.csv (sample telemetry), MAP-proposal.pdf (pilot economics), pilot-scope.docx (recommended test plan).

Proposed next steps (short timeline):
- Internal: Redwood to produce an SLO matrix and cost estimate for the 2-week pilot (Ben + Karthik) — deliver by Thu 6/17.
- External: Edgecase to share a representative sample dataset and preferred test windows (Jordan) — deliver by Wed 6/16.
- Schedule: kickoff for pilot the week of 6/21 pending approvals.

If this matches your understanding, I’ll shepherd approvals and credits on our side and Ben/Karthik can start sizing the runtime configuration.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@edgecase.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Edgecase AI — streaming SLOs, traffic profile & cost levers (pilot proposal)

Sean — good notes. A few engineering points / initial estimates: 
- For a 150ms p95 streaming SLO with 50 concurrent streams, conservative starting config is: 4x A100-equivalent slots with continuous batching enabled and 10ms batching window for latency-tolerant tokens.
- KV cache: per-customer in-GPU KV store will reduce compute by ~18-25% on repetitive prefixes (based on the sample).
- Quantization: int8 gives ~2.3x throughput improvement but expect small quality delta; recommend running an A/B on a curated prompt set.

I’ll produce a short SLO matrix with cost delta rows (continuous batching on/off, int8 vs fp16, model small vs base). Expect draft by 6/17 EOD and will attach kernel compatibility notes (kernel_matrix_v2.xlsx).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood

Sean, Ben — thanks for the clear summary. Couple clarifying items from our side: 
1) Traffic pattern: our internal telemetry suggests a baseline of ~180-220 rps with daily peaks that can spike to ~400 rps for up to 20 minutes when marketing pushes start. Spikes are generally predictable (campaign windows).
2) Dataset: we can share anonymized session logs and a 10k-prompt QA set by EOB 6/16.
3) Billing/pilot economics: do you have a rough per-day cost estimate for the 2-week pilot configuration you mentioned? We need to justify in our procurement.

Also — any limitations with token-level streaming when using int8 quantization? We want to avoid visible regressions in token timing.

— Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform, Edgecase AI

Subject: Re: Edgecase AI — streaming SLOs, traffic profile & cost levers (pilot proposal)

Jordan — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers and next-step items: 
- Pilot cost: Ben and I will model a conservative and optimistic cost column (int8 vs fp16; batching aggressive vs conservative). Rough back-of-envelope for 4x A100 slots with continuous batching: $1,200–$1,600/day (will refine in the SLO matrix). We can offset with trial credits — I’m requesting approval from finance now.
- Int8 & streaming: there’s no fundamental restriction on streaming with int8; main caveat is numerical differences can change token probabilities slightly. Recommend a small quality gate (sample-based) before enabling for production.
- Pilot plan: proposed 2-week pilot starting 6/21. Deliverables: SLO matrix, controlled A/B tests vs your QA set, perf telemetry capture, and a rollback/fallback policy.

Proposed concrete milestones:
1) By 6/17: Redwood sends SLO matrix + cost rows + kernel compatibility doc.
2) By 6/18: Edgecase uploads dataset + target test windows.
3) Week of 6/21: Kickoff pilot; first 48h smoke test; mid-pilot review 1 week in.

If agreeable I’ll raise the trial credit request and book a kickoff slot.

Sean

quick note from infra/compiler side: 
- Fallback policy: recommend a hybrid policy — prefer model routing first (small model) then graceful degradation to cached prefixes before throttling. This keeps UX intact during short spikes.
- Quantization caveats: int8 kernels look good for our target models but we should validate attention/scaling stability on your sample prompts; sometimes pathological distributions produce token-level artifacts. We should include a short regression suite as part of the pilot (can run in parallel).
- Kernel compat: attaching kernel_matrix_v2.xlsx (see Drive). Ben — please flag any GPU-local mem concerns for the 4x slot config.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Systems, Redwood
